title: Longest Common Subsequence
contract: Return the length of the longest sequence appearing in the same order in both strings; characters need not be contiguous.
optimal: int[] previous=new int[b.length()+1];for(int i=1;i<=a.length();i++){int[] current=new int[b.length()+1];for(int j=1;j<=b.length();j++)current[j]=a.charAt(i-1)==b.charAt(j-1)?previous[j-1]+1:Math.max(previous[j],current[j-1]);previous=current;emit("Finish one prefix row","prefix",a.substring(0,i),"row",previous);}return previous[b.length()];
reasoning: When characters differ, recursively skip one from either string; matching characters can extend a common subsequence.
dp[i][j] refers to prefixes of lengths i and j, with empty-prefix base values zero.
Keep the previous row and current left value. A longest common substring uses a different recurrence that resets mismatches to zero.
